claim: MML scores a hypothesis by total two-part code length (cost of stating the model plus cost of data given the model); it equals maximising Pr(H)*Pr(D|H), so it counts bits and needs no judge.
agent_test: Score candidate explanations by token length of explanation plus residual-error description; compare to a plain self-rating at equal tokens.
audit_note: Dowe 2010, Allison page and Wikipedia all give the two-part/Bayes identity; 'needs no judge' is an editorial gloss and MML is not the same as MAP in general.

claim: MML was first introduced for unsupervised clustering (Snob, Wallace and Boulton 1968); 1975 Strict MML, 1987 Wallace-Freeman formula. The founding paper itself was not opened by any agent.
agent_test: History only.
audit_note: Dowe foreword (1968 Snob with Boulton, 1975 Strict MML, 1987 with Freeman, 'repugnant'), Snob page and Wikipedia agree; the claim itself says the founding paper was not opened. Wikipedia/Allison/Dowe are not fully independent (Allison and Dowe are both Wallace's Monash colleagues).

claim: Parameter precision is part of the cost: the optimal stated interval has s^2=12/Fisher information, and over-precise estimates are over-fitting. Wallace-Freeman length = -log prior + neg log-lik + 0.5 log Fisher + constant.
agent_test: Penalise hypotheses that state precise values the evidence does not support; test calibration of stated precision.
audit_note: Dowe eq (20) and Allison Fisher page (s^2=12/F, +0.5 ln F) match; over-fitting statement is on Allison Inference page (same author lineage as Wallace, not fully independent).

claim: MML fixes maximum-likelihood inconsistency on Neyman-Scott (ML sigma^2 tends to (J-1)/J of truth; MML uses an N/(N-1)-style correction) and the Lancaster panel problem.
agent_test: Background; statistical, not agent-relevant.
audit_note: Dowe sec 6.4/6.5 and Allison normal-estimator code verified; Lancaster's own paper not opened, so the Lancaster claim rests on Dowe's statement (an MML advocate); N/(N-1) is the single-normal estimator, not the Neyman-Scott J-specific correction.

claim: In simulations by MML's own developers, MML beats AIC at order selection (polynomial ESPE 0.1857 vs 15.8 for AIC, N=10, 1000 cases) and on AR order, cyclone and von Mises estimation. Authored by MML proponents; no independent replication found.
agent_test: Run MML vs AIC vs BIC on a small model-selection toy; low priority.

claim: Recent applied MML papers report MML beating AIC/BIC/HQ for ARMA orders, model selection across families, and Granger graphs in sparse short series (F1 0.948 vs BIC 0.943 vs AIC 0.850, p=7, T=200; verified). Margin over BIC is tiny; all are small authored comparisons.
agent_test: Background.
audit_note: F1 0.948/0.943/0.850 at p=7,T=200 verified in the arXiv table; ARMA (Fang, Dowe et al.), species model-selection (Wen and Dowe) and Granger (Entropy 2020) abstracts verified via Crossref (MDPI pages returned 403); note two of the papers are by Dowe himself, so not independent of the MML group.

claim: Boundary: MML is not uniformly best. In denser graphs the MDL-based MDLH wins, ADM4 or thresholded ML beat MMLH at very short horizons, and at T>=1000 MMLH is below AIC and MDLH.
agent_test: Do not assume a compression score beats rivals everywhere.

claim: MML and MDL differ: MML is Bayesian with explicit priors and states all parameters in part one; MDL (NML, prequential) avoids priors. No head-to-head performance numbers exist in the sources read.
agent_test: Choose code type on practicality; see K09.
audit_note: Dowe sec 6.7, Allison page and Gruenwald 2004 tutorial support the Bayesian-vs-non-Bayesian distinction; 'no head-to-head numbers' is a statement about the sources read and holds for them; the MDL side is described by Gruenwald as avoiding a subjective prior, not literally as prior-free (prequential/Bayes mixtures use priors).

claim: Two-part and variational codes (MML lineage) are weak for neural networks: float32 two-part codes exceed the uniform code; variational code on MNIST gives 24.1 kbits (ratio 0.12, 95.5% acc) while prequential gives 4.10 kbits (ratio 0.021, 99.5%), 6x shorter. Re-verified in the PDF.
agent_test: Score reasoning by how well earlier steps predict later ones (prequential) rather than by stated-model length.
audit: downgraded 2026-11-20 by check_established.py: only 1 opened source(s) from distinct authors

claim: Shortest description alone can pick the wrong model: the best variational-code model gave 95.5% (MNIST) and 61.6% (CIFAR10) test accuracy versus 99.5% and 93.3% for prequential models.
schema_part: G (do not use compression as sole criterion)
agent_test: Check on our agent that the shortest explanation is not always the most accurate answer.

claim: Language models plus arithmetic coding are strong general compressors: Chinchilla 70B gives 43.4% on ImageNet patches and 16.4% on LibriSpeech versus PNG 58.5% and FLAC 30.3% (verified); LLaMA-7B reaches 0.71 bpc on text8.
agent_test: Background for the compression-prediction link.
audit_note: All numbers verified (43.4/16.4 vs 58.5/30.3; 0.7101 bpc); minor scope slip: the LLMZip 0.71 bpc is on a 1MB section of text8, not the full 100MB, which the paper says limits comparison with other methods.

claim: Charging model size (two-part code) removes the big-model advantage on small data: Chinchilla 70B adjusted enwik9 21.9% but ImageNet 185.3% and LibriSpeech 228.9% (verified); a critical model size exists per dataset. Prequential coding would charge less.
agent_test: Background.
audit_note: Adjusted rates (21.9/185.3/228.9), critical model size and prequential remark verified in Deletang et al.; Heurtel-Depeiges et al. (0.49 vs 0.54 FLAC) corroborate; 'removes the big-model advantage on small data' is a fair paraphrase.

claim: Bits per character on fresh text predicts average benchmark score almost linearly across 31 LLMs and 12 benchmarks (Pearson -0.93 knowledge, about -0.95 per domain, RMSE 3.1%; saturates near 3M characters; verified). Base models only. One paper counted from two agents.
agent_test: Cheap proxy for model quality; our agent is fixed, so not decision-relevant.

claim: MDL probing (online and variational code length) separates real linguistic structure from memorised control tasks: layer-0 control accuracy 96.3 vs 93.7 for the real task, yet codelength about 2x; accuracy picks the wrong task in 8 of 10 settings, MDL never (verified).
agent_test: Report solution length alongside accuracy when comparing agent configurations.

claim: Choosing in-context examples by shortest code length (MDL rank) raises mean accuracy to 60.16 vs 42.78 random and 58.14 TopK on GPT2-XL over 8 datasets (verified). Small model only; no test on frontier LLMs.
agent_test: Rank sampled candidate answers by model-assigned code length at equal tokens; compare with majority vote.

claim: In-context learning loss equals prequential code length, so ICL implicitly prefers simple models; GPT-4 failed to reduce prequential code length on a novel Mastermind task, worse than a small meta-trained transformer (qualitative, from figure).
agent_test: Measure whether our agent's per-step prediction loss falls across a task; the GPT-4 result suggests this is not guaranteed.

claim: Code-length objectives can drive reasoning-like systems: CompressARC trains a per-puzzle network on a code length with no pretraining and scores 20% (eval, pass@2) and 34.75% (train) on ARC in about 20 min per puzzle; the Kolmogorov Test finds frontier models poor at shortest-program generation.
agent_test: Use shortest-rule as a tie-break among ARC candidates; compare to frequency vote.
audit_note: CompressARC blog (34.75% train, 20% eval pass@2, ~20 min on RTX 4070, no pretraining) and Kolmogorov Test paper (78%/40% wrong programs, programs longer than gzip) verified; CompressARC source is a blog post, not peer-reviewed.

claim: Text compressed by an LLM is not learnable by a second LLM unless blocks are equal-information; compression and learnability trade off.
agent_test: Warning against compressing the scaffold's own memory too hard.

claim: No independent large replication or failed replication of MML itself was located in a limited search (arXiv, Crossref and web search were partly rate-limited); none of the LLM papers checked names MML (0 hits for 'message length' in Pan et al. 2025 and Huang et al. 2026, and an arXiv title search for 'minimum message length' language model returns only three non-LLM papers from 1997-2013). MML-in-LLM work is unestablished, while recent MML applications (e.g. Granger causality, ARMA-LSTM, species distribution models) exist outside LLMs.
agent_test: Treat MML as lineage, not as a tested method for LLM agents.
audit_note: Zero 'message length' hits in Pan et al. and Huang et al. and the 3-result arXiv search are verified, but 'the only 2025-26 AI paper using MML is a logic-program learner (d01)' has no listed evidence (d01 is not among the claim's sources; the arXiv search shows only 2012/2013/1997 papers) and is contradicted by Wen and Dowe (Entropy 2025, MML species-distribution model selection) which other claims here cite; the Allison page cited supports nothing about replication, and Elmoznino/Voita/Grau-Moya greps were not re-run.
claim_before_audit: No independent large replication or failed replication of MML itself was located, and none of the LLM papers read names MML (0 hits in Elmoznino, re-checked; Voita and Grau-Moya from agent grep). MML-in-LLM work is unestablished. Re-checked in the gap search: arXiv listings and full-text greps of five 2023-2026 LLM papers found 0 MML uses (d10, d11, d13, d14); the only 2025-26 AI paper using MML is a logic-program learner (d01).

claim: Strict MML is NP-hard in general (polynomial only for binomial); practice relies on the Wallace-Freeman approximation. Invariance and consistency are asserted by Dowe's group; Dowe's conjectures are unproven.
agent_test: None.

claim: An independent (non-Monash) head-to-head found an MML cost beats an MDL cost for learning logic programs at very small sample sizes and on one-sided data (size 1: +6.8%; positive-only +9.2%; negative-only +25.9%), but not on balanced or noisy data (no significant difference).
agent_test: When an agent learns a rule from 1 to 20 cases, charge over-general rules for what they fail to rule out.

claim: MDL-style compression helped LLM systems when it kept explicit structure: MIDGARD merge (+1.9 component F1, +2.0 R100 on gpt-3.5 macro average) and RIMRULE rule consolidation (+3.6 ToolHop, +4.5 BFCL over prompt-based consolidation). All are MDL, not MML, on small or older models.
agent_test: Compress the scaffold's rule memory with a length-plus-errors score and measure reuse on held-out tasks.

claim: Raw brevity is a bad score. A pure length penalty fell 10.94 points below vanilla GRPO on TextWorld-Cooking, while a dictionary (structure) cost gained +17.70 over it; MIDGARD's equal add and delete cost fell below greedy.
agent_test: Never rank answers by shortness alone; combine with fit and recurrence.

claim: A pure code-length solver on ARC reaches 20% eval pass@2 (CompressARC, 20 minutes per puzzle) or about 6-7% (MADIL, no LLM); both are far below LLM approaches, so the shortest-rule rule is at best a tie-break. No test of that tie-break against frequency voting was found.
agent_test: Run shortest-rule tie-break versus frequency vote on ARC items as an ablation.
audit_note: CompressARC (20% eval, 34.75% train, 20 min) and MADIL (7% ArcPrize 2024, 6.0% private; paper says below LLM methods, LLMs 55%) verified; the 20% is on the public eval set and MADIL's 6-7% on the private set, so they are not like-for-like, and 'at best a tie-break' is the author's inference.

claim: No study was found that tests ranking sampled final answers by model code length against majority vote or self-rating at equal tokens on a frontier LLM (gap 1), or that tests prequential versus two-part scoring on reasoning traces (gap 2), or that links claim precision to calibration (gap 6).
agent_test: These are open experiments for the bench harness.

claim: Wallace and Boulton 1968 full text (data, class counts, 10-bit thresholds) was not accessible; only the abstract (SNOB on KDF 9, agreement with conventional taxonomy) was read.
agent_test: None; use a generic accept-if-total-shorter stop rule.

claim: No independent MML versus AIC/BIC replication was located, but the search was cut short by rate limits.
agent_test: Treat the MML advantage over AIC/BIC as developer-reported.
